disclosures.name: TestRuneCountNonASCIIAllocation
disclosures.reason: NEW at 1.24: a want-zero AllocsPerRun over `s := []byte("日本語日本語日本語日"); _ = RuneCount(s)`. Go's escape analysis keeps the []byte(const) conversion and RuneCount's slow-path string on the stack, so it asserts zero; the converted path charges 3 per run. DEFERRED, not alloc-count-semantics: the run's own unit note says `counted 30 go2cs-runtime object allocations ... over 10 run(s) ... an allocation COUNT per run` -- Go's own unit, so the counter saw them. The three sites, each read in golib at the 1.24.13 hop: (1) the test's []byte(const) -> slice<byte> from a span -> AllocationCounter.CopyOf; (2) RuneCount's non-ASCII slow path `RuneCountInString((@string)(p[n..]))` -> @string(slice<byte>) -> ToArray -> CopyOf; (3) ranging over that @string -> RuneSpanEnumerator, a class charged by AllocationCounter.Count(). (2) and (3) are LOCAL to RuneCount and removable; (1) is the escape-analysis class no local change removes, hence the floor. RE-READ AT go1.26.10 (2026-10-25, G): reading moved from 3 per run at go1.24.13 to 1 per run on windows and linux; the test body is identical at go1.24.13 and go1.26.10.
disclosures.reading: 1 per run on windows and linux -- go1.26.10 at d804094d7a (batch 37's tip), Release with tiering off; windows: 10 go2cs-runtime object allocations (560 bytes) over 10 runs, alloc-units-windows.tsv line 188 (claude/g-pass2-plan 966562828d); linux: 10 go2cs-runtime object allocations (560 bytes) over 10 runs, alloc-units-linux.tsv line 175 (claude/p1-alloc-reading 8d9d880ca2); both TSVs under docs/phase4/data/rebank-go1.26.10/; unit COUNT, a LOWER BOUND
disclosures.plan: a byte-walking RuneCount slow path that counts rune starts over the byte span without materialising a @string or a rune enumerator (a hand-owned body, or the converter emitting builtin.tmpstring for a string(b) passed to a callee that does not retain it -- golib's existing zero-copy alias for exactly that contract). That removes sites (2) and (3); the entry then reads 1 per run, which is its floor.
disclosures.proof: site (1): the test body's []byte(const) is a non-escaping conversion Go keeps on the stack, and the managed model must copy the literal into a fresh byte array (slice<byte>'s span constructor -> AllocationCounter.CopyOf) because a Go []byte is mutable storage the receiver owns. Falsified by a run reading 0 per run with the counter still charging slice<byte>'s span constructor.
